scope: local mathematical research; selected statements mirrored in a live private Prove2me mission; note proofs are not Lean-verified

conventions.parameters: even integers n >= 2; p=9, m=n, deg W <= 4
conventions.norm: weighted Euclidean norm with coordinate weights (1,n^2,n^4,n^6,n^8)
conventions.area: Delta_n=covolume of the saturated low-zeta kernel K_n in the weighted norm

nodes.title: Irrationality of zeta(9)
nodes.statement: The real number zeta(9) is irrational.
nodes.obstacle: No uniform asymptotic control of the second independent integer form is proved.

nodes.title: Infinite subsequence with exponential margin
nodes.statement: There exist epsilon>0 and infinitely many even n>=2 such that B_n+sigma_n <= 10.564-epsilon.
nodes.obstacle: Need to rule out eventual stabilization of the actual primitive first-output direction; finite direction changes and the new exact area exponent do not establish this.
nodes.known_equivalence: Under the now-proved V and actual polynomial-denominator connection, J is equivalent to irrationality, to liminf sigma_n=0, and to infinitely many primitive first-output direction changes. No one of these open conditions is proved.

evidence.section: Polynomial transport and equivalence, not a proof of J

nodes.rational_branch: For every fixed (b,a) with a nonzero, log(h_n/q_n)=o(n). If zeta(9) is rational, B_n+sigma_n tends to alpha=0.5 log A > tau and liminf sigma_n > 0.33493507; this is compatible with all proved bounds.

nodes.title: Critical second-minimum polynomial margin
nodes.statement: With alpha=-f_*, T_n=n^5 exp(alpha n), Z_n=sum_(k>n)R_n(k), and lambda2_n the weighted second minimum of Z^2 E_n W_n, liminf over even n of lambda2_n/T_n is zero. Equivalently, by the proved kernel asymptotic, liminf lambda2_n Z_n=0.
nodes.obstacle: The inverse-area spectral upper bound and Smith lattice formulas do not control the first lattice direction relative to Xi_n Z_n; no infinite sequence with this critical second-minimum margin is proved.
nodes.new_structure: Actual second mode is now proved nonzero. Complete-output minima have exact rational/irrational conditional exponent branches; no branch is selected unconditionally.

evidence.section: Exact ellipse and conditional minima dichotomy

nodes.title: Infinitely many positive full-lattice first directions
nodes.statement: For infinitely many even n, at least one nonzero shortest vector z E_n of the integer-output lattice Z^2 E_n has its coefficient polynomial in the Taylor cone at u0=(n+1)(2n+1): all five Taylor coefficients have one weak sign.
nodes.obstacle: The first vector has a real root in (u0,infinity) at frozen n=24 and n=192; finite positive cases do not establish infinitely many positive first directions.

nodes.title: Infinitely many saddle-signed full-lattice first directions
nodes.statement: There exists a fixed A>0 and infinitely many sufficiently large even n such that at least one shortest nonzero integer-output vector z_n E_n has a coefficient polynomial P_n whose sampled values P_n(k(k+n)) have one weak sign for every integer k>n with |k/n-x_*|<=A(log n)/sqrt(n), where x_* is the unique positive-kernel saddle.
nodes.obstacle: The uniform signed-saddle lemma proves nonvanishing once the sign condition holds, but no infinite sequence of moving shortest integer directions satisfying it is known.

nodes.title: Infinitely many five-sample-signed first directions
nodes.statement: For infinitely many sufficiently large even n, at least one shortest nonzero vector z_n E_n of the full integer-output lattice has a coefficient polynomial P_n whose five values P_n(k_(n,j)(k_(n,j)+n)), j=-2,-1,0,1,2, have one weak sign, where k_(n,j)=floor(n x_*+j sqrt(n/a)+1/2), a=-f''(x_*) and x_* is the unique positive-kernel saddle.
nodes.obstacle: The five-point cubature gives nonvanishing whenever this sign condition holds, but no infinite arithmetic theorem controls the moving shortest lattice direction at these five prescribed points.

nodes.title: Infinite endpoint-denominator height criterion
nodes.statement: For infinitely many sufficiently large even n, [lambda1(E_n) ||(1,0)E_n W_n||_2 / Xi_n] (h_n-ell_n) min(Q_-,Q_+) <= 1, where ell_n=P_-/Q_- and h_n=P_+/Q_+ are the reduced five-sample rational endpoints with positive denominators, Xi_n=area(Z^2 E_n W_n), and lambda1(E_n) is the weighted first minimum.
nodes.obstacle: The five-sample width contracts exponentially, but no uniform upper bound for the reduced endpoint denominators and actual first-vector height proves this product condition on an infinite sequence.

nodes.title: Infinitely many positive partial-lattice first directions
nodes.statement: For infinitely many even n, at least one shortest nonzero v_n in Lambda_{g_n} has a nonzero coefficient polynomial whose five Taylor coefficients at u0=(n+1)(2n+1) have one weak sign.
nodes.obstacle: The five frozen g_n Gauss first directions have one sign, but no infinite subsequence or eventual sign theorem is known.

nodes.title: Subexponential congruence-lattice shape defect
nodes.statement: As even n tends to infinity, sigma_n tends to 0; equivalently log(mu1(Lambda_g_n)/sqrt(g_n Delta_n))=o(n).
nodes.obstacle: Must exclude every primitive kernel direction that is exponentially shorter after its exact congruence multiplier; finite Gauss reductions do not suffice.

nodes.title: Full formal coefficient map and inverse image
nodes.statement: For every even n>=2, F_n is invertible over Q. For each integer output (b,a), the inverse image w=(b,a)S F_n^{-1} gives the exact form L_n(w)=b+a zeta(9), with lower odd-zeta coefficients zero.

nodes.title: Uniform positive-moment exponential bound
nodes.statement: For every even n and every rational coefficient vector w of degree at most four, |L_n(w)| <= exp((-10.564+o(1))n) sum_{r=0}^4 |w_r| n^(2r), where the o(1) is uniform in w.

evidence.section: exact rational interval certificate

nodes.title: Smith image and second-minimum bound
nodes.statement: For every even n>=2 and divisor g of N_n, Z^2 E_n=(D_n/s2_n)Lambda_N_n and lambda2(E_n) <= (2/sqrt(3))(D_n/s1_n)Delta_n/mu1(Lambda_g), all in the same weighted Euclidean norm.

nodes.title: Two independent integer forms criterion
nodes.statement: If on infinitely many indices two Q-linearly independent integer pairs (b_i,a_i) have both |b_i+a_i zeta(9)| tending to zero, then zeta(9) is irrational.

nodes.title: Positive one-form criterion and first-vector lift
nodes.statement: A nonzero integer-output coefficient polynomial with one weak sign in its five Taylor coefficients at u0 has a strictly nonzero positive-kernel sum. If such integer-output vectors have weighted norm at most exp((10.564-epsilon)n) for infinitely many even n, then zeta(9) is irrational. A shortest v_n in Lambda_{g_n} lifts to z_n E_n=(D_n/(s1_n g_n))v_n with log norm/n=B_n-sigma_n.

evidence.section: positive-kernel proof and exact Smith lift

nodes.title: Eventual positivity of the two-step Taylor connection
nodes.statement: The exact normalized Taylor transfer H_n satisfies H_n H_(n+2) -> H^2 with all 25 entries of H^2 strictly positive. Consequently every fixed real output (b,a) with b+a zeta(9) nonzero has all five Taylor coefficients eventually of that output sign. In particular the two coordinate Taylor rows are eventually positive, and their min-max ratio intervals contain zeta(9), strictly nest along each residue class modulo four, and satisfy limsup log(interval width)/n <= (1/2)log(|lambda2|/lambda1)<-10.1109, where lambda1 and lambda2 are the two largest-modulus roots of the proven limiting connection polynomial.

nodes.title: Uniform signed-saddle nonvanishing lemma
nodes.statement: For every predetermined positive window sequence h_n tending to zero with n h_n^2/log n tending to infinity, every sufficiently large even n, and every nonzero real quartic q, one weak sign of q(k(k+n)/n^2) at all k>n with |k/n-x_*|<=h_n forces its infinite positive-kernel sum to be strictly nonzero with that sign. In particular h_n=A(log n)/sqrt(n) for any fixed A>0 is valid. Consequently an infinite sequence of exponentially short integer outputs with this sampled sign proves irrationality of zeta(9).

evidence.section: uniform Stirling, five-sample interpolation and infinite-tail proof
two finite full-lattice signed-sum certificates

nodes.title: Gaussian saddle moments and sharp constant window
nodes.statement: For the actual positive kernel R_n(k), the normalized moments of the affine-in-y saddle coordinate s_(n,k)=sqrt(a n)(k(k+n)/n^2-y_*)/(2x_*+1), orders 0 through 4, converge to (1,0,1,0,3). Let A_c=sqrt(3/a), where a=-f''(x_*) and 0.095251<A_c<0.095252. For each fixed A>A_c, every sufficiently large even n and every nonzero real quartic q with one weak sign at all actual samples |k/n-x_*|<=A/sqrt(n) has a strictly same-sign full infinite positive-kernel sum. For each 0<A<A_c there are moving rational quartics that are positive throughout this continuous window but have negative full sum. The equality case is not asserted.

evidence.section: Gaussian moment limit, compactness, sharp counterexamples and rational threshold
exact rational threshold and limiting moment checks

nodes.title: Eventually positive exact five-sample cubature
nodes.statement: For all sufficiently large even n, choose k_(n,j)=floor(n x_*+j sqrt(n/a)+1/2) for j=-2,...,2. There are five strictly positive weights omega_(n,j), summing to one and independent of q, such that for every real quartic q the exact identity sum_(k>n) R_n(k) q(k(k+n)/n^2)=Z_n sum_(j=-2)^2 omega_(n,j) q(k_(n,j)(k_(n,j)+n)/n^2) holds. Thus weak agreement of the five signs for any nonzero moving quartic forces a strictly same-sign complete infinite sum.

evidence.section: section 6, finite Vandermonde inverse and positive limiting weights
exact limiting five-node Gaussian moments

nodes.title: Abstract geometry alone does not force five-sample signs
nodes.statement: For every sufficiently large even n there is a rank-two integer polynomial lattice whose every nonzero vector has both a positive and a negative value among the three prescribed samples k_(n,-2), k_(n,0), k_(n,2). After common integer scaling, its weighted first-minimum logarithmic rate and weighted-area logarithmic half-rate both tend to 5, below the established corresponding upper bounds. This is an abstract counterexample to a geometry-only implication, not a counterexample for the actual E_n output lattice.

evidence.section: three-point sign contradiction and exact weighted-area bounds

nodes.title: Strict five-sample ratio interval and slope criterion
nodes.statement: For all sufficiently large even n, the five rational sample ratios r_(n,j)=q_(n,(0,1))(y_(n,j))/q_(n,(1,0))(y_(n,j)) have positive denominators and define a nondegenerate interval ell_n=min_j r_(n,j)<zeta(9)<h_n=max_j r_(n,j), strictly inside the Taylor coefficient ratio interval. Its width has limsup logarithmic rate below -10.1109. For every nonzero integer output (b,a), five-sample weak sign agreement is equivalent to a=0 or -b/a outside the open interval (ell_n,h_n); strict sign agreement uses the closed interval. This does not prove the infinite shortest-vector condition T5.

evidence.section: strict positive cubature average, Taylor convexity, and endpoint criterion

nodes.title: Uniform approximation by every first output
nodes.statement: Let A=lambda_1>0 and B=|lambda_2| be the top two eigenvalue moduli of the actual limiting Taylor connection, and delta=(1/4)log(A/B)>5.05545. For every epsilon in (0,delta), all sufficiently large even n, and every weighted first output (b,a) of Z^2 E_n, a is nonzero and |b+a zeta(9)|<=exp(-(delta-epsilon)n); consequently |-b/a-zeta(9)| obeys the same bound. If zeta(9)=c/d is rational in lowest terms, every sufficiently late first output is exactly one of +/−(-c,d).

evidence.section: sections 1-2, positive moment column, Perron lower bound, Hermite upper bound, and rationality lock

nodes.title: Exact five-endpoint denominators and integer gap
nodes.statement: For all sufficiently large even n, put A_n=d_n^9 F_n, C_n=S adj(A_n), and Ctilde_n=C_n/delta4star_n. At each of the five sample integers t_(n,j), the ratio r_(n,j)=Ctilde_A v(t)/Ctilde_B v(t) has reduced denominator Q_(n,j)=|Ctilde_B v(t)|/gcd(|Ctilde_B v(t)|,|Ctilde_A v(t)|). If an integer output (b,a), a!=0, has slope -b/a strictly inside (ell_n,h_n), then |a|(h_n-ell_n)>1/min(Q_-,Q_+). Every first output also satisfies |a|<=lambda1(E_n)||(1,0)E_n W_n||_2/Xi_n. Hence the product condition in FD at any eligible n forces every first output to have weak one-sign values at all five samples.

evidence.section: sections 1-2, adjugate endpoint formula, integer separation, and exterior-product height bound

nodes.title: Same-limit rational connection can fail five-sample sign
nodes.statement: For every sufficiently large even n, a rational full-rank alternative Taylor connection can be constructed with the actual five prescribed sample nodes, a strictly positive exact five-node cubature, positive moment column, eventually positive two-step transfer, and the same limiting spectrum H and inverse-area upper exponent as the actual construction, but with rational output value theta and eventual first outputs exactly +/−(-c,d) mixed-sign at the five samples. It is an obstruction only to a proof using those structural consequences alone; it does not preserve the exact actual finite-parameter connection C(n).

evidence.section: section 3, rational alternative connection and eventual zero-relation first output

nodes.title: Exact actual inverse-area exponent and uniform first-output height bound
nodes.statement: For the actual recurrence, lim log(Xi_n)/(2n)=(1/4)log(A B), where A and -B are the two dominant eigenvalues of G. The exact rational invariant cone holds for all real n>=20 and contains the actual F20 wedge. Every complete output lattice first vector (b,a) satisfies limsup log(max(1,abs(a)))/n <= (1/4)log(A/B) < 5.05562. Combined with the proved arithmetic bound, limsup B_n < 10.394861.

nodes.title: Critical second-minimum irrationality equivalence
nodes.statement: For the actual positive kernel and full output lattice, Z_n is asymptotic to C_Z n^(-5)exp(f_*n), both fixed coordinate rows have norm Theta(n^5 exp(-f_*n)), and zeta(9) is irrational if and only if lambda2_n=o(n^5 exp(-f_*n)), if and only if liminf lambda2_n/[n^5 exp(-f_*n)]=0. Equivalently, lambda1_n/(Xi_n Z_n) tends to infinity. Under rationality zeta(9)=c/d in lowest terms, liminf lambda2_n/[n^5 exp(-f_*n)]>=1/(d C_Z ||v_*||)>0; the unique late first direction is +/−(-c,d), lambda1_n lambda2_n/Xi_n tends to one, and lambda1_n/(Xi_n Z_n) stays bounded above and below by positive constants. This is a criterion and does not establish its open short-vector hypothesis.

evidence.section: sections 1-3, positive moment row bounds, rank-one collapse, Diophantine dichotomy, and Minkowski comparison

nodes.title: Determinant and minor-gcd identities
nodes.statement: For every even n>=2, det F_n=((3n/2)!(7n/2)!)/(7n((n/2)!)^10). With A_n=d_n^9 F_n and minor gcds delta3_n,delta4star_n, N_n=|det A_n|delta3_n/(delta4star_n)^2 and N_n divides d_n^45 d_(7n/2)^8.

nodes.title: Weighted area of a saturated integer kernel

nodes.title: Intermediate-prime merged-pole bound
nodes.statement: For every even n>=2 and prime sqrt(7n/2)<p<=n, write m=floor(n/p), K=7m+9, and define the merged-pole moments M_{a,k}(W) as in the evidence for every integer polynomial W of degree<=4. Every M_{a,k}(W) lies in p^(7m) Z_(p); if p>K, 1<=k<=K, and (k-1)p<7n, then sum over a mod p of M_{a,k}(W) lies in p^(7m+1) Z_(p). Also v_p(N_n)<=30+D_np-5h_np<=38, where D_np is the exact determinant valuation residual and h_np=1 if 3(n mod p)>=2p-1 and 0 otherwise. Consequently for fixed H>1 the contribution to E_mid from p<=n/H has limsup rate at most 27/H.

nodes.title: Primitive-direction congruence formula

nodes.title: Intrinsic local congruence slope
nodes.statement: For every even n>=2 and divisor g of N_n, M_n=J_n/s1_n is integral with Smith factors (1,N_n), and Lambda_g={zK_n:zM_n=0 mod g}. A primitive direction has multiplier g/gcd(g,content(zM_n)); for each p^e|g the local condition is one dot product against any column of M_n containing a p-adic unit. Globally Lambda_g is the row lattice generated by the rows of gI_2 and adj(M_n), then multiplied by K_n.

reductions.qualification: CP is the still-open critical lattice estimate; CM is a proved equivalence that does not by itself establish irrationality.
T is an open infinite sign assertion; the proven area bound alone only yields one short vector.
SP controls every tail and proves nonvanishing, while TS is an open infinite sign assertion for moving short lattice vectors.
Exact positive cubature proves nonvanishing after five signs are known; T5 remains an open infinite assertion about moving shortest lattice vectors.
TG and V together bypass S; five positive first vectors do not imply TG.
V and S are stronger than J; failure of either does not refute J.
The five predetermined samples eventually lie in every fixed A log(n)/sqrt(n) saddle window; TS is stronger than T5.
FD is a sufficient infinite arithmetic criterion, not necessary for T5; FC proves only the pointwise integer-gap bridge.
VA is a sufficient arithmetic strengthening; its failure does not refute V or J.
VB is a sufficient prime-valuation budget; its failure does not refute VA.
VD retains exact valuation discounts and is weaker than VC; it remains open.
VC is a sufficient intermediate-prime strengthening; its failure does not refute VB.
